text.p: These are the leading stories in Belgrade press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.

- U.S. Assistant Secretary of State John Kornblum says U.S. welcomes Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic's invitation for an Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe mission to visit Serbia.
- Less than ten percent of Serbia's projected 14 billion dinar 1997 budget ($2.74 billion) will go to finance economy.
- Nis district court annulled Nis electoral commission decisions and insructed it to reexamine results within ten days.
- Montenegro parliament to elect new government of the republic at its session Monday.
- Street protests continue in Belgrade and other Serbian cities. The truth on November 17 election results is a condition for talks, say opposition leaders.
- Serbian export-import firm Genex plans organisational and ownership transformation and has entrusted Belgrade office of Deloitte & Touche with the job.
- The fall in the value of the domestic currency on the blackmarket has been halted and the dinar is not expected to drop further for a period.
- Annual inflation in 1997 is expected to drop to below 15 percent if a similar environment to this year's is maintained, says Serbian Deputy Prime Minister Svetozar Krstic.

- Belgrade shipyard is building seven ship hulls for Holland worth 8.5 million German marks and is working on restoring business ties with old partners in Sweden, Norway, Germany, Libya etc., says director Milenko Krsmanovic.

- German mark drops in Sremska Mitrovica. Street dealers are buying the mark for 3.3 and 3.4 dinars (official exchange rate is 3.3 dinars. Last week, the DM was worth up to four dinars on the Black Market).
